senses.definition_en: to give a name to something

usage_example.sesotho: Motho a reha liphoofolo tsohle tse ruuoang mabitso le libopuoa tse fofang le liphoofolo tsohle tse hlaha empa motho eena o ne a se na mothusi ea mo tšoanelang.
usage_example.english: So the man named all the domestic animals and the flying creatures of the heavens and every wild animal of the field, but for man there was no helper as a complement of him.

senses.definition_en: soft tissue of the body; meat

usage_example.sesotho: Monna a re: “Joale enoa ke lesapo la masapo a kaLe nama ea nama ea ka. O tla bitsoa MosaliHobane o nkiloe ho monna.”
usage_example.english: Then the man said: “This is at last bone of my bonesAnd flesh of my flesh. This one will be called Woman,Because from man she was taken.”

senses.definition_en: to depart from or abandon

usage_example.sesotho: Ke ka lebaka leo monna a tla siea ntate oa hae le 'mè oa hae 'me a khomarele mosali oa hae, bobeli ba bona e tla ba nama e le 'ngoe.
usage_example.english: That is why a man will leave his father and his mother and he will stick to his wife, and they will become one flesh.

senses.definition_en: any of the pieces of hard whitish tissue making up the skeleton

usage_example.sesotho: Monna a re: “Joale enoa ke lesapo la masapo a kaLe nama ea nama ea ka. O tla bitsoa MosaliHobane o nkiloe ho monna.”
usage_example.english: Then the man said: “This is at last bone of my bonesAnd flesh of my flesh. This one will be called Woman,Because from man she was taken.”

senses.definition_en: without clothing; nude

usage_example.sesotho: Ka bobeli ba ile ba tsoela pele ba hlobotse.
usage_example.english: And they were both naked.

senses.definition_en: to cease work or movement in order to relax or recover strength

usage_example.sesotho: Molimo a hlohonolofatsa letsatsi la bosupa 'me a re lea halalela hobane letsatsing leo o ile a phomola ka mor'a mosebetsi oohle oo a o entseng.
usage_example.english: And God went on to bless the seventh day and to declare it sacred, for on it God has been resting from all the work that he has created, all that he purposed to make.

senses.definition_en: a cloud of tiny water droplets suspended in the atmosphere

usage_example.sesotho: Empa moholi o ne o nyoloha fatše 'me o nosetsa lefatše lohle.
usage_example.english: But a mist would go up from the earth, and it watered the entire surface of the ground.

senses.definition_en: fine, dry powder consisting of tiny particles of earth

usage_example.sesotho: Jehova Molimo a etsa motho ka lerōle la lefatše.
usage_example.english: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground.

morphology.derivation: Deverbative noun from the verb 'phefumola' (to breathe)

senses.definition_en: the air taken into or expelled from the lungs

usage_example.sesotho: A bululela linkong tsa hae phefumoloho ea bophelo.
usage_example.english: And breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.

senses.definition_en: a large number of people or things; army

usage_example.sesotho: Rorisang Jehova, lona mabotho 'ohle a hae,Lona basebeletsi ba hae, ba etsang thato ea hae.
usage_example.english: Praise Jehovah, all his armies,His ministers who do his will.

senses.definition_en: a woody plant which is smaller than a tree

usage_example.sesotho: Ho ne ho e-s'o ka ho e-ba le lihlahla le limela lefatšeng hobane Jehova Molimo o ne a e-s'o nese pula 'me ho ne ho se na motho ea ka lemang.
usage_example.english: No bush of the field was yet on the earth and no vegetation of the field had begun sprouting, because Jehovah God had not made it rain on the earth and there was no man to cultivate the ground.

morphology.derivation: Common noun for a cultivated plot

senses.definition_en: a piece of ground, often near a house, used for growing flowers, fruit, or vegetables

usage_example.sesotho: Ho ekelletsa moo, Jehova Molimo a lema serapa Edene, ho elella ka bochabela 'me a beha motho eo a mo entseng teng.
usage_example.english: Further, Jehovah God planted a garden in Eʹden, toward the east; and there he put the man whom he had formed.

morphology.derivation: From 'chaba' (to rise, of the sun) + 'ela' (applied suffix)

senses.definition_en: the direction towards the point of the horizon where the sun rises

usage_example.sesotho: Lebitso la noka ea boraro ke Hidekele, ke eona e eang ka bochabela ho Asiria. Lebitso la noka ea bone ke Eufrate.
usage_example.english: The name of the third river is Hidʹde·kel; it is the one going to the east of As·syrʹi·a. And the fourth river is the Eu·phraʹtes.

senses.definition_en: a large natural stream of water flowing in a channel to the sea, a lake, or another such stream

usage_example.sesotho: Joale ho ne ho e-na le nōka e tsoang Edene ho nosetsa serapa seo.
usage_example.english: Now a river went out of Eden to water the garden.

senses.definition_en: a yellow precious metal, the chemical element of atomic number 79

usage_example.sesotho: Khauta ea naha eo e ntle. Ho na le mamina a sefate a nkhang hamonate le lejoe la onikse moo.
usage_example.english: The gold of that land is good. Bdellium gum and onyx stone are also there.

senses.definition_en: facts, information, and skills acquired by a person through experience or education

usage_example.sesotho: Empa ha e le sefate sa tsebo ea botle le bobe, u se ke oa ja litholoana tsa sona hobane letsatsing leo ka lona u li jang, kannete u tla shoa.”
usage_example.english: But as for the tree of the knowledge of good and bad, you must not eat from it, for in the day you eat from it you will certainly die.”

senses.definition_en: hard solid non-metallic mineral matter of which rock is made

usage_example.sesotho: Khauta ea naha eo e ntle. Ho na le mamina a sefate a nkhang hamonate le lejoe la onikse moo.
usage_example.english: The gold of that land is good. Bdellium gum and onyx stone are also there.
